fields.v: Spec-anchored (judgement; the authors do not classify their own framework). The paper cites spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source for Spec Kit, Kiro and Tessl; it describes its specifications as 'verifiable contracts' and SDD specifications as 'versioned, auditable, and executable sources of truth', and targets maintenance and evolution with traceability metadata, which suggests spec-anchored. Spec-first is also plausible, since spec.md, design.md, plan.md and tasks.md are generated per task (e.g. adding a status field)
fields.ai: Not classifiable (closest: spec-anchored). The paper cites spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source for Spec Kit, Kiro and Tessl but does not classify its own framework; it describes specifications as 'verifiable contracts' and SDD specs as 'versioned, auditable, and executable sources of truth', and targets maintenance and evolution with traceability metadata

fv.prev: Spec-achored. The paper cites spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source for Spec Kit, Kiro and Tessl but does not clearly classify its own framework as spec-anchored; it describes is own specifications as 'verifiable contracts' and SDD specs as 'versioned, auditable, and executable sources of truth', and targets maintenance and evolution with traceability metadata what induces in a Spec-achored way.
